meta.title: Slab — From 41 minutes to 9: fixing our CI
meta.description: Engineering talk from Slab, a construction-scheduling platform: CI took 41 minutes because every pull request rebuilt and retested all 140 packages. A remote build cache and eight-way test sharding cut the median to 9 minutes. Evidence, mechanism, config, trade-offs and one takeaway.

slides.heading: Our CI took 41 minutes. Cache and shards made it 9.
slides.notes: Twenty-minute slot. About one slide a minute; give the config slide three.

slides.heading: Build and tests ate 31 of every 41 CI minutes
slides.lead: Every pull request rebuilt 140 packages and ran 1,840 test files on one runner.
slides.imageAlt: Pipeline bar for a median pull request: checkout 2 minutes, install 6, build 14, test 17, lint and upload 2, with build and test highlighted as 31 of 41 minutes

steps.body: Why was CI doing so much work?
How do cache and shards remove it?

slides.heading: Why was CI doing so much work?
CI time grew 2.6× in a year as the repo doubled
slides.lead: Source: GitHub Actions run history, 61,000 pull-request runs. Packages grew from 70 to 140.

slides.heading: A typical pull request changed 3 packages and rebuilt all 140
slides.body:
CI had no memory between runs.
Unchanged code was built and tested again from scratch.
slides.imageAlt: Grid of 140 package squares with 3 highlighted as changed and 137 labelled rebuilt anyway

slides.heading: How do cache and shards remove it?
Eleven lines: reuse unchanged builds, split tests across eight runners
slides.code:
test:
  strategy:
    matrix: { shard: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8] }
  env:
    TURBO_API: https://cache.slab.internal
    TURBO_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.TURBO_TOKEN }}
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
    - run: pnpm turbo run build --filter=...[origin/main]
    - run: pnpm vitest run --shard=${{ matrix.shard }}/8
slides.notes: Two ideas. TURBO_API points every runner at one shared cache, so a package built once is downloaded, not rebuilt. The shard flag splits 1,840 test files into eight equal slices by past timing.

slides.heading: Median CI fell from 41 minutes to 9, and p95 from 63 to 14
slides.left:
Build 14 min
Tests 17 min
Median 41 · p95 63 min
slides.right:
Build 2 min · 94% cache hits
Tests 4 min
Median 9 · p95 14 min

slides.heading: Speed cost 59% more runner minutes and one new way to fail
We would put the toolchain version in the cache key on day one
slides.body:
Both stale hits came from a Node upgrade the key ignored.
Both shipped an old build to staging.
slides.aside: Fix: hash the Node, pnpm and OS versions into every key.

slides.heading: Stop rebuilding what has not changed. Split what has.
slides.lead: 41 minutes became 9. The workflow and shard timings are open source.
slides.notes: Close on the sentence, then give the repo URL from the notes: github.com/slab-eng/ci-cache.
